steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Plate tectonics states the lithosphere is divided into large plates that move on the asthenosphere, driven by convection currents in the mantle

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Divergent boundaries: plates move apart (e.g. Mid-Atlantic Ridge), creating new oceanic crust

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Convergent boundaries: plates collide; oceanic-continental produces subduction zones and volcanoes; continental-continental produces fold mountains

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Transform boundaries: plates slide past each other (e.g. San Andreas Fault), causing earthquakes

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the three types of plate boundary? | Q: What evidence did Wegener use to support continental drift? | Q: How does paleomagnetism support seafloor spreading?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Three boundary types: divergent, convergent, transform Wegener's evidence is commonly tested, know at least 3 lines of evidence Paleomagnetic striping is key evidence for seafloor spreading, symmetrical about the ridge Subduction: denser oceanic ALWAYS sinks beneath lighter continental
